item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Aquí Hubo Escena: Aquí Hubo Escena
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Page Layout: Looking to use a format similar to those of SCP-4028, SCP-3020 and SCP-3031. Audio files if possible.

Elevator Pitch: A memetic agent starts spreading across finished musical compositions. Depending on the fame, the listener's perception and the themes the piece touches, this agent can cause all sorts of benefitial or detrimental changes on a person's body and psyche. Although the agent starts propagating on niche music spheres, it eventually reaches mainstream hits.

Central Narrative: Trough different evidence we learn about our PoI, an anomalous individual who was heavily involved in his country's music scene. In naive attempt to improve his situation and the one of his fellow companions, he ends up risking up the veil and getting the community he so much loved killed (both metaphorically and literally). After barely surviving lynching and escaping persecution, he releases the memetic agent with ambiguous motivations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the fact this skip deals with a not so explored topic, this entry has the intent of confronting the Foundation with a fundamental dilemma: is it really better to live on your knees than to die on your feet? Is the Foundation really willing to declare a war on artistic expression for the greater good?.

Additional Notes: It's Intended to be a connection between our PoI and the GoI "Deer College", this may change in the future.

item.title: mysterious blackmail: Re: mysterious blackmail
item.content:encoded:
do you think I should get rid of the negative feelings thing?

Yes. In my response above, the paragraph starting with "So far as content goes, I'm not a fan of the premise since it relies heavily on a compulsion effect" covers why I don't think that effect helps your piece.

hey can you check if there is anything else I could delete there is the possible cause the materialization of the envelope

I'll be honest, right now it looks like you're focusing on the smaller details that don't really matter than much (envelope materialization) without addressing the bigger issues that are the more major roadblock to your concept being workable.

So far the revisions don't really address what I mentioned previously; in fact the premise is worse than the previous iteration because you've introduced more severe and overpowered effects that don't make sense. It's still unclear why the blackmail setup operates the way it does (did you take into account fraudulent charities? Redundant charities? Legitimate charities with leaders who embezzle money?). Additionally, the anomaly forcing people to give up what they have to the point where they beg for money and steal items to donate causes more problems, which ironically many charities try to prevent.

I think you might want to take a break from this idea for a little while and come back to it with fresh eyes. The recent edits you've made admittedly seem haphazard and not well thought-out.

Also, out of curiosity, have you read many Series V and Series VI SCP articles? The approach you're using here looks like it takes inspiration from Series I articles, which aren't usually the best example of current site expectations for quality and content.

item.title: Origami Brain: Re: Origami Brain
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a quick look.

+ show block
– hide block

I'll be honest, I immediately am iffy on the core anomaly because it combines two extremely commonly seen formulaic approaches ("thing that kills in an oddly specific way for no reason" and "thing that forces people to act a certain way") and the only narrative background is "AWCY? is involved somehow". I'm also skeptical that an AWCY? anartist would expect someone to consistently unravel the brains of the individuals who died from the anomaly just to see some hint at an indication of affiliation.

At any rate, even if the message you've got in mind is something that I can see an AWCY? anartist spreading, the fact that the videos were apparently targeting children really doesn't sit well with me and I would downvote pretty immediately for the gratuitous violence. Given that a real-life child has died after attempting to follow a DIY-type video (Ann Reardon's video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CEQaYdvs478 discusses the matter quite well, I think) the approach you've used feels somewhat tactless to me as a reader.

There's also the rather unnecessarily callous Foundation response:

Follows some investigation logs, a series of testings to discover details about the anomaly (how much of the video one must watch to become affected, how long the symptoms take to appear, how long it takes to die, etc)

If it's clear that exposure to the anomaly causes test subjects to die, the Foundation has no reason to continue testing something like this. The Foundation has no reason to assume that the information of how long it takes for an individual to die due to the anomaly is even close to worth a test subject's life, let alone the lives of multiple test subjects.

Overall… I'm not sure this is workable as currently presented. I myself wouldn't be interested in reading a full draft of this unless it were basically rewritten to address the following:

  • don't make the anomaly just kill people. If you really want to write body horror, have there be something more unique than just "it kills people by turning part of their body into something else"
  • have the motive of the anomaly's creator be clearer and more relatable. Thus far the generic and kind of stereotypical "art is dead, here is a reminder of what true art is" message intended to be spread through the deaths of innocents feels both disingenuous and hypocritical. How can this person expect people to grow artistically if they're killing said people before that growth can occur? And for those who are observing the effects, wouldn't that just discourage them from ever attempting origami on their own?
  • address the fact that sometimes people just watch the videos for inspiration, or because they're bored, or because they want to try something out. Not everyone watches content farm material because they think the channel needs support or because they feel like a patron of the arts. People who genuinely don't know about why content farms are bad shouldn't be punished for happening to watch a video posted by a content farm.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights): Lullaby lady: (Seeking Greenlights): Lullaby lady
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: An entity that resembles a female corpse that puts children under the age of 8 to coma. The entity hunts families with a child under the age of 8. It mysteriously crawls out of closets or drawers inside the victim's house at approximately 1~2 o'clock midnight. Then proceeds to sing a
"Lullaby". The lullaby affects children to wake up from their sleep immediately, but gives a counter effect to adults which puts them to deeper sleep. The child(victim) who lacks a guardian is held firmly by the entity, unable to resist. After the lullaby is over, the entity kisses the victim's forehead which makes the victim fall in a coma. The entity then disappears from the house only leaving a fowl, garlic scent.

Central Narrative:The article is narrated based on a interview between Scp agent "Joshua" and Robert, the only victim known to recover from the coma. The interview provides gruesome description
of the entity itself and events that happen inside of the coma.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: All victims in the state of coma are to be euthanized for it is the most ethical treatment the Foundation can provide. Also, the containment procedures involves animal sacrifices, torment and more unethical procedures which gives the reader curiosity of the Scp and it's powers.

Additional Notes:Thank you so much for reading and I really hope to see reviews!!

item.title: Hydrophobic Fountain: (Seeking Greenlights) Hydrophobic Fountain
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient fountain that doesn't want to be played in or climbed on creates hydrophobia-inducing water.

Central Narrative: School-kids on their senior year start spreading a local legend among their younger peers and other people to not to interact with a certain fountain. One day, a pipe of the fountain is burst by the fountain, spreading a town’s water supply, creating a hydrophobic town.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fountain itself and its experience as a structure that's always been alive for years.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea that already has a draft, as it was liked by many reviewers back when it was first made, both in IRC chatrooms and forum posts. (This draft is about 2-3 years old.) I took a long hiatus from skip writing, but I may be returning to finish this skip. I wonder if the idea itself has aged well, but I might as well see if it gets greenlit so I can advance it towards the draft forum and hope to get it published soon. Despite trying to write skips 2-3 years ago, am I still considered a first-time author?

item.title: Dionysus Asylum: Dionysus Asylum
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: an insane asylum with anomalous properties that helps people with their mental issues and is often used by the foundation to contain entities that aren't mentally stable.

Central Narrative: the article mostly focuses on excerpts from a journal written by a foundation MTF agent, who was held captive by the Asylum because he suffered from PTSD after an encounter with another dangerous anomaly. the journals talk about how the agents experience within the asylum, as well as encounters with other patients, most of which happen to have anomalous properties. Eventually the agent begins to comply with the treatment and is soon released from the asylum.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the asylum possesses multiple anomalous items such as straitjackets that induce drowsiness on anyone who wears them. the Asylums staff are completely invisible except for their brains and nervous systems, and it's implied they're all part of some kind of hive mind. The asylum itself also possesses anomalous properties, such as appearing like an abandoned building to anyone who hasn't been through/is suffering from psychological trauma or mental illnesses. Despite keeping most of it's patients there against their will, the Asylum really does just want to help people.

Additional Notes:I think given the nature of this SCP and how the foundation uses it it'd probably be a Thaumiel but I'm not entirely sure. I also considered the asylum being immune to reality warping but I'm not too sure about that either.

item.title: Matter alterning SCP: Re: Matter alterning SCP
item.content:encoded:
The idea is interesting, but your concerns about it being similar to SCP-294, SCP-914, and other experiment-log-based articles are accurate- your first task with this idea will be finding a way to make an old concept feel fresh and new. That said, heavily scientific SCPs are some of my personal favorites, and they can be a lot of fun when done well.

What I would suggest is focusing the idea down a little- say, make it a specific piece of lab equipment that can carry out some impossible reaction you find interesting. Just like a sublimation tube or autoclave can be used to conduct many different reactions, a device with a single well-defined impossible property can make many impossible experiments possible. (Simply being able to freely convert materials between phase states and crystal arrangements would be enough to create some bizarre materials and reactions- metallic hydrogen foil, crystaline neon, gaseous sodium, liquid tungsten carbide… I'm honestly not sure if room temperature solid F2 would be more or less terrifying than the normal sort…)

Modern SCPs are are also very focused on storytelling within the format- Funnily enough, one SCP that's similar to this idea is one I wrote, SCP-2871 (Strong Interaction Amplifier), and I think it makes a decent example of one way to approach this in science-heavy articles: The anomaly in 2871 is a device that modifies the Strong Nuclear Force to cause nuclei to fuse at normal temperature and pressure- the story is why the containment procedures forbid operating version 1.0 of the device.

item.title: Eurotrash: Re: Eurotrash
item.content:encoded:
I wont deny that I've recently become kind of enamored with the UIU myself, which is a big part of why I thought this would be fun. To address your questions, though -

As to the character interactions (which, I agree, are going to be what sells the story even moreso than my attempts at writing mystery or action). To that end, I've been kind of working out my thoughts for the team.

So far the character clearest in my mind is "Droopy" Drummond, the team leader, who earned the nickname due to an outlook on the edge between 'realistic' and 'pessimistic' after his experiences in the UIU ("We have excellent bereavement benefits" and all that). In fact, in my head, his first question when asked to investigate this scenario is "Shouldn't we be passing this on to the Skippers?"

With a guy like that, I'll probably need a more outgoing and eager sort to balance him out (I'm thinking at least one "rookie" recently transferred to the UIU who has an outlook that there's nothing that enough effort and/or bullets can't deal with).

The remainder of the group… well, probably following the classic Four Temperaments wouldn't be a bad idea. I will admit that, as it is, for the group as a whole I was thinking of some fairly pulp-style characters (so "men/women of action" types who may grouse and complain about it and bicker incessantly, but will get things done). The best comparison I could think of would be "Doc Savage's aides without Doc Savage".
If possible and the story actually survives, I would like to use them as recurring characters for adventures (again "Pulp" so why not make them into a series of weird happenings?)

In the end, I'm a "Good Guys win" sort, so my ending as it stands would be the group does/should succeed and either capture or… eliminate the Aristocrat infestation. As this would be their first story together, I'd probably use it as the means to have them gain traction together and finally cooperate well enough to do the job.

item.title: SCP Idea, needs greenlight: Re: SCP Idea, needs greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hey there MemesAtLarge, I'll be critting your idea today!
This is going to be a relatively brief crit, so here goes:

Your pitch, while intriguing, unfortunately comes across as just another version of those trippy shapes. They both incorporate entities from a higher-dimensional plane, they both made contact with people for knowledge, and they both appear in the form of shapes. In my opinion, your idea is just too similar to succeed on the Site without being pegged as a clone of SCP-2634. I'd recommend either heavily reworking or potentially even scrapping this idea, due to the similarities and therefore immense difficulty in successfully executing this idea on the mainsite.

I also recommend two more things:
1. Check out the Guide Hub for some great essays on ideation and story-ing!
2. Contact someone from the Butterfly Squad for some alternative opinions from experienced reviewers!

Anyway, thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

item.title: [Seeking Greenlight] : Gnome Tree: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
As per the Draft Forum Policies found here: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies

Site members who can greenlight concepts are those who fulfill one or more of the following criteria:

  • They are on the Butterfly Squad Roster list of reviewers.
  • They have an entry in the Authors' Pages list or they qualify for an Author Page (they have written 3 or more successful mainsite pages).
  • They have been featured in the Reviewers' Spotlight.
  • They are a staff member.

You may want to consider messaging users listed from above to see if they'd be interested in looking at your concept. Also, reviewers would usually make it obvious when they greenlight something (such as stating that they are giving the concept a greenlight).

item.title: Echos eines Hoffest: Echos eines Hoffest
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History

Page Layout (Optional): Video logs, interviews, document references and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: The city of Mainz (Germany) gathers annually during the Pentecost day for a party in which the citizens anomalously change their behaviour as if they were in the 12th century for a day. After an incident, the Foundation intervenes only to provoke this change to become permanent.

Central Narrative: During the Pentecost day in Mainz, its citizens celebrate the festivity in a nearby location, where upon access they show an altered behaviour proper of the European nobility in the 12th century, such as a firm code of honour; and participate in joust tournaments. By the following day, citizens involved have no related memories.

+ Show
- Hide

This activity went under the radar of the Foundation until a Turkish attendant was found dead after one of these events with the words "Deus Vult" engraved on his chest. The following year, Foundation found out about these effects with on-site live-recordings. Identifying a potential assault similar to the previous year, a task force bursts into the gathering, disbanding all attendants. This time affected individuals keep their memories and the behaviour displayed during this event. Chaos ensues due to the cultural clash with modern Germany.

The next Pentecost day, affected population gathers again, live-recordings showing that the activities performed are exactly the same as in the previous year. Once the celebration finishes, all attendants return to the normal behaviour. Foundation decides not to interrupt this event, but stops population from attending by fencing the site. Instead, attendants move to nearby Ingelheim, where anomalous natural catastrophes result in hundreds of casualties. The Foundation allows the event to occur at the usual location, however impeding the attendance to vulnerable individuals.

Recording logs interview seemingly a monk, who seems to be responsible of these events. Back in 1184, Kaiser Barbarossa hosted a huge fest in that same location. By law, Konrad was to be seated by the Kaiser during the ceremonies, however he was substituted in a political move by the Archbishop of Cologne. Resentful, he condemned the dishonour, ensuring that that day would be repeated over and over until the Kaiser rectified his mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is a story about timely cultural clash, by bringing a huge population from the past to the current days. It is also a story about resentment and, literally, holding a grudge.

Additional Notes: Based on the 1184 Mainzer Hoftag. Kaiser Barbarossa might be SCP-125-DE.
